Taxonomic classification of the most complete bins with GTDB-Tk. Commands for this step were run in `gtdbtk/`.

## **Step 6: Perform taxonomic classification with gtdbtk**

 change directory to the `gtdbtk` folder.

```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/gtdbtk
```

First just get the while loop working

```{bash}
while read bin;do echo $bin;done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

We need to turn this bin name into a path specifying the fasta file for the bin. So for every bin we need to prepend the path to its folder `../metabat/bins_bbd/` and then append the file extension `.fa`

```{bash}
while read bin;do echo "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa";done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

Now we are ready to perform the copy

```{bash}
while read bin;do cp "../metabat/bins_bbd/${bin}.fa" genomes;done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
```

Check that it worked by listing files within the `genomes` directory. You should see one file for each of the bins

```{bash}
ls genomes
```

create a blank shell script file and save it inside your `gtdbtk` directory. Name your file `run_gtdbtk.sh`

```{bash}
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=120
#SBATCH --ntasks=2 --mem=56gb

echo "Starting gtdbtk in $(pwd) at $(date)"

shopt -s expand_aliases
alias gtdbtk='apptainer run -B /pvol:/pvol,/pvol/data/mg/gtdbtkdata/release207_v2/:/refdata /pvol/data/sif/gtdbtk.sif'

gtdbtk classify_wf -x fa --cpus 2 --genome_dir genomes --out_dir out --skip_ani_screen

echo "Finished gtdbtk in $(pwd) at $(date)"
```

Submit the job:

```{bash}
sbatch run_gtdbtk.sh
```

It is done so now i can check that it produced a summary classification

```{bash}
ls -l out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv
```

it did get created

copy the summary up into the `gtdbtk` folder. Git ignores everything inside `out`, but it can see a `.tsv` file saved directly in `gtdbtk`, so this lets you add the summary to your repository.

```{bash}
cp out/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv .
```
